title: Ophan polish
eyebrow: Options for the five follow-ups from your play-through of the Ophan redo (#468)

short.lead: Your play-through found the redo working: it chases, breaks the castle, and takes the artifact to spare you. Five things are left: the door plugs that do not break, the triangle count for the Steam Deck, telling a killing beam from a sparing one, the open gap inside a broken wall or floor, and guards walking over holes. Each has options with my suggestion marked.
short.hint: Tap an item to see what I found and what it needs from you.
items: Why door plugs do not break

ProceduralCastleGenerator places door plugs, the solid blocks that close an unused doorway, beside the rooms rather than inside them. The charged beam only names rooms (CastleRoomModule), and the step that splits rooms into parts and the bake step only looked at room prefabs, so plugs are never split, baked or hit.
Nothing to pick: plugs get the same split, bake and hit as rooms.
How to fit the Steam Deck

The bake subdivides every part to 0.75 m pieces: 3,083,428 triangles over the 79 room types, a mean of 39,031 per room against 1,044 before. Doubling the piece size to 1.5 m cuts the count to about a quarter, because halving the piece size turns each triangle into four, so doubling it leaves a quarter.
Pick a budget (Choices, "How should the triangle count come down?").
Telling the kill from the spare
Today the beam is the same warm white whether it is about to kill you or about to take your artifact and spare you.
Pick a tell (Choices, "How should a sparing beam look different?").
Why a hole shows a gap inside the wall

A wall or floor is a front surface and a back surface with empty space between them (0.5 m for walls, 0.3 m for floors). The break removes pieces from both surfaces, so through the hole you see the empty space between them, as in your pictures of the floor.
Pick how the gap is closed (Choices, "How should holes be capped?").

Guards path on the castle's own navigation grid, built once when the castle is made. Nothing tells the grid when a floor breaks, so its cells over the hole still count as walkable. The grid can mark a cell unwalkable at run time (CastleNavGrid.ClearWalkable).
Pick what the grid learns (Choices, "What should guards know about breaks?").

changes: Split, baked and hit by the charged beam
RoomPartSplitter and CastleFractureBake now include plugs, and the charged beam names any castle piece on its line, not only rooms.
Code touched: CastleFractureBake (budget), OphanLook (beam), the fracture hit (caps), the castle navigation grid (guards).
choices: How should the triangle count come down?
1.5 m pieces, and props stay whole

Walls, roofs, floors and plugs are subdivided to 1.5 m instead of 0.75 m, and props are not subdivided (they break as whole pieces). I measure the new total from the bake and put it on the next QA page.
The same 1.5 m for every part, props included. Simpler, but props cost triangles they gain little from.

Bake no subdivision at all; the host subdivides the area around each hit when it happens and sends nothing extra. Fewest triangles, but each break adds work in the frame it happens, and the fracture graph (which pieces hold which up) has to be rebuilt at that moment.
Option A keeps breaks looking the same at a quarter of the triangles for walls, and props never needed small pieces.
How should a sparing beam look different?
When the target carries what it wants, the beam turns gold, the game's colour for loot, and its pulse slows. A beam meant to kill stays white-hot and pulses faster through the charge.
The killing beam turns a deep red through the charge; the sparing beam stays warm white.
Same colour; a slow pulse for the take and a fast one for the kill. The subtlest option.
Gold already means loot in this game, so a gold beam reads as "it wants your treasure" without teaching anything new.

When a hole is broken, every edge it leaves is joined front to back with a strip of the wall's own stone, so the hole shows a solid broken edge 0.5 m deep, or 0.3 m in a floor. Every machine builds the same strips.
Draw the inside of walls and floors dark, so the gap reads as shadow. Cheaper, but you can still see into it at an angle.
Option A makes a broken wall look solid, which is what your pictures were missing.
What should guards know about breaks?
When a floor part breaks, the host marks the grid cells over the hole unwalkable, so guards path around it. Broken walls open no new routes for guards.
Holes, and new routes through walls
As A, and a hole through a wall big enough to walk through also joins the cells on both sides, so guards can chase through it.
Option A stops guards walking on air; new routes through walls can follow if you want guards using them.

wrapup.summary: Five follow-ups from your play-through: door plugs, the Steam Deck triangle budget, a tell for the sparing beam, capping holes, and guard paths over holes.
wrapup.changing: Nothing until you pick. The redo stays as it is on AjsAgent/gym-with-demand-page.
wrapup.blocking: Your picks for the triangle budget, the beam tell, hole caps and guard paths. Also say whether the redo itself passes QA as it stands.
wrapup.next: I file the issues, build your picks in order, record the co-op run and read it before it reaches you.
